scope: Read-only actual diagnostic/provenance review and prospective test-only design. No workload, source/test/helper/dependency edit or prior capture rewrite. One new review written.

actual_diagnostic.limit: Instrumentation did not reproduce the original false lease probe; it can perturb race timing. Successful attempts include local/preparatory ownership calls, not nine independent crash-release trials. No full-suite equivalence, denial cause or product immunity is established.

original_failure.assertion: Dead controller retained its lease after repair barrier
original_failure.cause: Unproven: original evidence does not distinguish parent owner registry, FIFO gate or native lock denial. No product leak confirmed and no external/antivirus cause proven.

authoritative_contract.claim: The OS unlocks byte ranges on process termination/handle close; completion delay depends on available resources and access may remain denied until release.
authoritative_contract.implication: Immediate nonblocking acquisition following process.wait is a stronger test assumption than documented native eventual release.
authoritative_contract.limit: Documentation justifies reviewing the assertion contract independently; it does not diagnose this failed candidate capture or map its unrecorded rejection branch.

prospective_design.conditional_scope: Only hard-crash integration test/helper assertions; no application locking/API behavior, frozen86/gold evaluator, worker workload or timeout widening.
exact_steps: At every noncomplete persisted crash barrier, confirm child remains alive and prove another fresh UoW cannot acquire its controller lease; check child is still alive before terminating.
Record absolute termination_deadline=time.monotonic()+30 immediately before first process.kill. Do not reset it on cleanup kill.
Use process.wait(timeout=remaining_positive_time) against the same deadline; no independent new30s wait allowance.

After process exit, attempt fresh UoW timeout0 controller acquisition only while original remaining budget is positive. On false, close failed UoW normally and sleep at most min(original20ms polling interval,remaining); retry only as a bounded test observation of eventual OS release.

Accept acquisition only if the call and context cleanup complete before the same deadline. Record elapsed postkill observation; never accept a late result merely because probe started before deadline.
Fail persistent contention, wait expiry, ownership/exclusion failure or unexpected exception. Keep all subsequent exact state/event-prefix/effect-deduplication/delivery/recovery assertions unchanged.
Complete phase retains original successful process exit behavior; no extra controller polling needed.
prospective_design.test_helpers: Prefer a small test-only callback/helper using the existing factory/run_id with fresh UoW per probe, so the exact original long controller lease API remains the subject. No registry clearing, lockfile deletion, native-only bypass or success from a different run/path.
prospective_design.budget: Original180s child barrier budget remains untouched. Postkill wait and release observation share original30s budget; borrowing180s or adding30s release wait is rejected.
counterexamples_required: A live controller incorrectly allowing another owner makes the test fail before kill.
A native release delayed after exit succeeds only inside remaining original deadline and still uses real controller API.
A controller lock never released fails at deadline, not pass after repeated label/rerun.
Process wait consuming nearly/all30s leaves only remaining/zero probe allowance; overall release observation cannot become wait30s+poll30s.
A successful lock attempt completing after deadline fails and releases the acquired lease; original state/effect/history assertions cannot be skipped.
Unexpected acquire/release errors remain visible; no swallowed ownership or corruption errors.
prospective_design.description_required: Call this a prospective platform-aware test contract correction, not proof the original failure was OS delay or a repaired product regression.
